title: Migration 64 — a document review decision must name its reviewer
description: Applies migration 64 to the bootstrap substrate, runs its VERIFY A-E, then rolls it back on a disposable PostgreSQL cluster. public.farmer_documents could record that a certificate was accepted and when, but not by whom -- the same defect migration 63 closed on status_history, in the one place it matters most, because an accepted certificate is the decision a buyer ultimately relies on. 64 adds reviewed_by, forces it from auth.uid() by trigger so a caller cannot attribute their decision to a colleague, and adds review_decision_requires_reviewer so no route to a decided state can skip it. Section C is the point and runs as a SUPERUSER with auth.uid() NULL: it must be REFUSED, which is also why a service-role or cron process cannot move a document out of pending -- the project's standing rule is that only an authorised human decides, and this is that rule expressed where it cannot be bypassed.

verify.note: C is the assertion that matters and it runs as a superuser on purpose -- a rule that only binds the application layer is a convention, and this one must bind whatever reaches the table. B guards the subtle failure: the trigger fires only when review_status actually changes, so a later extraction writing lab_name must not restamp a decision made by someone else at another time. Without B, a trigger that fired on every UPDATE would still pass A, C and E. D proves returning a document to the queue clears the attribution rather than leaving a reviewer named as responsible for a decision that no longer stands. E proves the SECURITY DEFINER trigger function is not directly callable.
